noah (sdk): heads up — hit a puzzling TS typing regression after switching our edge sample to ESM build + esbuild. works fine in CJS.
noah (sdk): minimal example in the SDK:
```ts
// public API
export function getBlob(id: string): Promise<string>
export function getBlob(opts: { id: string; binary: true }): Promise<Uint8Array>
export function getBlob(arg: any) { /* impl */ }
```
noah (sdk): locally with node16 resolution and tsc produces correct overloads in .d.ts. after our esbuild ESM pipeline (emitDeclarationOnly + isolatedModules) consumers get only the first overload in the published .d.ts. callers who pass { binary: true } still infer string.
leah (ts): that rings a bell — TypeScript sometimes collapses overloads when declarations are emitted without a full program context. isolatedModules + declaration emit is fragile. bundlers can reorder/transform files in ways tsc's emit assumptions break.
sam (devex): this breaks a few onboarding examples where we demonstrate binary vs string responses. we should avoid subtle API shapes that depend on overload pick-order if consumers build with ESM/bundlers.
leah (ts): quick diagnostic: generate the .d.ts locally with tsc (moduleResolution: node16, no isolatedModules) and compare to the published package. if they differ, the build step is the cause. also grep for `declare function` ordering.
noah (sdk): did that — tsc-built d.ts has both overloads in order. esbuild-generated d.ts (via api wrapper) collapsed them. Repro in gist: https://gist.github.com/anon/ef56c9 (package.json, build script, tiny src).
leah (ts): immediate fixes:
- prefer a single discriminated generic overload for public API to avoid relying on overload ordering
- or have a dedicated tsc declaration step (tsc -p tsconfig.declarations.json) with moduleResolution: node16 and emitDeclarationOnly: true (and isolatedModules: false)
noah (sdk): lean toward doing a dedicated declaration build. want to be careful about CI times but we can cache.
sam (devex): also add a note in the SDK README about recommended tsconfig for publishing (we've seen `moduleResolution: bundler` break emitted declarations in few projects).
leah (ts): another caveat: `unknown` vs `any` in public overloads — some consumers using `--declaration` and `skipLibCheck` may get widened types when `unknown` is used inside conditional types. If we use discriminated unions + explicit generics it's more stable across toolchains.
noah (sdk): interesting — we had a spot where `unknown` in a generic conditional made inference fail for edge runtimes. switching to `any` fixed the inference for some users (ugh). but `any` reduces type safety.
leah (ts): I'd recommend documented pattern: expose a user-friendly wrapper with narrow types, keep internal helpers with `any` if necessary. And in d.ts build step avoid `isolatedModules` and set `moduleResolution` to node16/nodeNext depending on target.
noah (sdk): filed issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2468 with repro and suggested CI change (declaration build). CC: @sam
ci-bot: created issue #2468 by noah (sdk) — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2468 :robot_face:
sam (devex): i'll add a checklist item for sample templates + runner to ensure they publish with a stable d.ts. also will update the onboarding guide with a short section on "ESM build gotchas".
noah (sdk): thanks! quick patch in the sample app switching the public API to a single generic overload to keep examples consistent until CI change merges.
leah (ts): happy to review proposed type changes. in longer term we should include a declarative test that verifies published d.ts shape (small script comparing tsc emit to package d.ts).
